question: The school marching band logs its rehearsal time in minutes rather than in hours. On Monday the band rehearsed for 147 minutes, and on Tuesday for another 72 minutes. Wednesday's session ran 80 minutes and Thursday's ran 72 minutes. On Friday, when half the band arrived late, they still managed 45 minutes. At the end of the week the director split the total rehearsal time into 4 equal blocks, one block for each piece of music. How many minutes long was one of those blocks?

Priya scored 154 points in the first round of a video game tournament. A double-points power-up she picked up made her round total grow to 2 times its size. She then lost 64 points when a hidden trap wiped out part of her combo streak. Her rival, Jonas, had scored far fewer points overall and was already out of contention for the finals. In the bonus round, Priya earned 3 more points for a perfect combo. A final multiplier event for the top players made her total grow to 8 times its size. What was Priya's final score?

A manufacturer had 102 units. They multiplied by 5 for production. Then by 3 for doubled shifts. Then by 3 for team assignments. Then by 6 for facility capability. Finally, they multiplied by 3 for expansion planning. They subtracted 12138 units from a major order. Between James (production lead) and Alice (planning), how many units remain?

A store started with 236 items. They subtracted 90 for sales. They added 17 from restocking. They subtracted 64 more for another sale. They added 40 from a delivery. Maria had 200 items at her store but unrelated. After initial sales and restocking but before the second sale, how many items remained?

Early in the morning a market gardener cut 81 bunches of stocks. Each bunch was tied from 9 stems. Every stem carried 3 open flowers when it was cut. In the afternoon a helper brought in 48 more flowers from the polytunnel. Just before closing that evening a customer returned 23 flowers that had not fitted in her vase. How many flowers does the gardener have altogether?

Tara has collected 232 bottle caps, which she keeps in a dozen glass jars. Her sister Uma has 9 times as many bottle caps as Tara, so Uma's collection is much larger. Over the summer Uma found 40 caps at the beach, 32 caps at a festival, and 36 caps behind the corner shop. She then handed 1954 caps over to a recycling drive. How many bottle caps does Uma have now?

A ferry company had 212 life jackets in its store. An inspection condemned 17 of them as worn out. Another 42 went down to the small boats at the jetty. The summer fleet then took 144 more out of the store. A repair shop returned 12 jackets it had mended, and a supplier delivered 23 new ones. The ferry carries 180 passengers, and the crew logs its safety drills in minutes rather than hours. How many life jackets are in the store now?

The charity shop had 181 second-hand books on its shelves at the start of the week. Donations brought in 75 more books on the Tuesday. A dozen volunteers take turns behind the till. A clearance sale on the Saturday sold 255 books to a dealer who arrived with a van. The manager sent whatever was left to a printer, who produced 7 copies of it for the hospital reading group. Of those copies, 4 were given away at the first meeting. How many copies did the reading group still have?

A water company tracked consumption with unit conversion. Starting with 89 cubic meters, residential added 68 (157). Commercial added 53 (210). Industrial added 58 (268). The total was multiplied by 6 for monthly projection. Converting to millions of liters, this represented about 1.6 million liters monthly. What was the monthly volume?

A vending machine's coin box held 163 cents at the start of the school day. During morning cleanup, the janitor removed 93 cents to fix a jammed slot. He then split what remained evenly between 2 identical collection jars and kept only one jar. That afternoon, the office manager added 58 cents in cafeteria change to the jar, and later the school store contributed another 56 cents. For the bank deposit, the treasurer made 8 identical envelopes, each holding that same jar amount, and combined them into one total. Since 100 cents equal 1 dollar, the school always double-checked its coin counts. How many cents did the treasurer send to the bank?

A charity had 64 boxes of supplies to distribute. They split the boxes equally among 4 communities. They again split equally among 4 homes per community. They multiplied by 7 to account for family sizes. They multiplied by 3 for donation drives. They added 19 emergency boxes. They had 100 volunteers. How many supply boxes were distributed?

A supply chain had 123 items at opening. In the morning, the count multiplied by 7. By midday, 28 items were used. The inventory multiplied by 7 for the afternoon count. By evening, 48 more items arrived. Finally, 3762 items were shipped out for distribution. How many items remained in stock?

A phone's battery showed 88 percent charge when Nina left for her hike. During the first hour, streaming music drained 29 percent. Taking photos on a scenic overlook used another 22 percent. A long phone call on the way down cost her 36 percent more. Since her phone reports charge in percent, which is just battery-minutes converted to a fraction of 100, she never worried about the raw units. When she got home, her charger's fast-charge mode brought her battery up to 6 times its drained level before bed. Overnight, a scheduled optimization further pushed it to 5 times that amount by morning. What percent charge did Nina's phone show the next morning?

Gus has collected stickers for a dozen years. He had 138 stickers and gave 110 of them to a younger cousin. At a swap meet he traded each remaining sticker for a pack of 4 stickers, and then found 5 loose stickers in his bag. His album has 20 pages. He gave 53 stickers to his friend Hal, who now has fewer stickers than Gus. In the club contest every sticker is worth 9 points, and Gus also earned an 18-point bonus. How many points does Gus score?
A task had 19 hours. Added 36. Multiplied by 5. Added 18. Then 26. Multiplied by 5. Added 12. Supervisor allocated 7 assistant. How much total?

A theater sold 200 tickets by the morning box office opening. By midday, 141 tickets had to be refunded after a show was postponed, and an afternoon promotion made the remaining tickets grow to 5 times its size. Since the box office counts tickets individually but the accountant reports revenue in whole dollars, the manager kept both figures on separate sheets. That evening, 164 more tickets were refunded for a second cancellation. A late rebooking event made that total grow to 3 times its size. Overnight, 45 tickets were voided due to a printing error, and a final morning rush made the remaining tickets grow to 7 times its size. How many tickets did the theater have after that final rush?

The council planted 204 flower beds in the park last autumn, and 6 tulips went into every bed. Half of the beds lie along the edge of the lake. A hard frost in February killed 221 of the tulips. The parks team replanted 45 tulips in the gaps as soon as the ground softened. The park itself covers 15 hectares. Every tulip that flowered opened with 8 petals, and the show display in the glasshouse contributed 79 further petals to the count. How many petals were counted in the park?

Tom started with 17 marbles. His friend Alex had 100 marbles. Tom won 57 marbles in a game. He then lost 55 marbles. He found 11 marbles on the street. He doubled his collection. He doubled it once more. How many marbles does Tom have?

A business had 191 dollars. They added 55 dollars. They divided by 6. They added 3 dollars. They removed 11 dollars. Morning transactions, afternoon deposits, evening balance. 500 dollars elsewhere. How much money?

A manager had 187 tasks. They removed 185, leaving 2. They added 49, reaching 51. They added 14 more, reaching 65. They added 40 additional, reaching 105. They removed 101, leaving 4 tasks. How many tasks remain?

A warehouse had 224 bicycles in stock, tracked over 120 minutes, or 2 hours, of inventory, even though the warehouse has 15 loading bays. A shipment removed 80 bikes for a big order. A delivery added 76 more bikes. Five more matching shipments made the total six times as large. Finally, 907 bikes were shipped out to stores. How many bicycles were left in the warehouse?

A budget started at 147 dollars. In the morning, 58 dollars were spent. By noon, 16 dollars were refunded. By afternoon, 10 more arrived. Then 114 dollars were withdrawn. By evening, the remaining tripled and was converted to fifty-cent units (unit change). How many fifty-cent units?

A village hall fund receives 219 dollars every month from the parish council. After 5 months the committee spent 917 dollars on a new roof. A raffle then added 57 dollars to the fund, and a bake sale added 62 dollars. How many dollars are in the fund now?

A savings account started with 191 dollars. They withdrew 180 dollars. They added 62 dollars. They doubled the balance (multiplied by 2). They subtracted 98 dollars in fees. They added 45 dollars in interest (converting dollars to cents). By afternoon, he had earned 50 dollars more in other accounts. After withdrawal and adding 62, how much remained?

A tea factory puts 53 bags into every packet, and each box holds 4 packets. A case is filled with 5 of those boxes, and one case was set aside for a hotel. A worker added 42 loose bags to that case, and then 229 bags were found damp and thrown out. The factory has been running for 70 years, and half of its staff work nights. Each bag left in the case makes 9 cups of tea, and every cup holds 3 ounces, since the hotel measures its drinks in ounces rather than in pints. How many ounces of tea can that case make?
